title: Human redistribution of host plants expands butterfly resource geography largely independently of diet breadth

central_claim.text: Human redistribution of larval host plants substantially expands butterfly resource geography across the specialization spectrum. Host-family breadth has little relationship to proportional gain, while the added opportunity is strongly concentrated among a minority of contributing host plants. A secondary occurrence analysis shows that introduced-host geography recovers contemporary butterfly observations missed by native-only host envelopes beyond region-matched expectation.
central_claim.support_type: global resource reconstruction + unit-preserving host-contribution decomposition + diet-breadth precision/equivalence diagnostic + ceiling/regional/taxonomic/phylogenetic robustness + secondary species-cluster occurrence validation

claims.claim: Human redistribution of host plants broadly expands butterfly resource geography, while family-level diet breadth has little relationship to proportional gain.
claims.status: primary macroecological result with post-hoc precision/equivalence, finite-area, regional, random-effect and species-level phylogenetic sensitivities
claims.evidence: 239 butterflies in the full reconstruction; 207 species in the strict host-bias null; 8,909 host plants in 278 families in the plant-level analysis; 124 exact Kawahara-tree butterfly species in PGLS.
claims.key_statistic: 206/239 butterflies expanded; aggregate species×WGSRPD3 coverage +54.9%; full-panel Spearman rho=0.008, 49,999-bootstrap 95% CI -0.111 to 0.128; ±0.10 Fisher-z TOST p=0.078 (equivalence not established); Family random-effect beta=0.021, p=0.752; estimated Pagel lambda=0.033 with rank-PGLS beta=-0.051, p=0.581; fixed Brownian beta=0.140, p=0.119.
claims.phylogenetic_sensitivity: Kawahara exact-species subset n=124 is selective for higher expansion magnitude. Estimated Pagel lambda=0.033 and rank-PGLS beta=-0.051 (95% CI -0.234 to 0.131, p=0.581). Fixed Brownian lambda=1 gives beta=0.140 (95% CI -0.036 to 0.317, p=0.119), so moderate positive effects remain unresolved under that boundary model.
claims.null_parameter_sensitivity: 3×3 grid: degree exponent 0.5 retained a host-identity excess across all native-range bandwidths; exponent 1 largely attenuated it; exponent 2 produced null expansion greater than observed. Attribution to host choice versus prominence is therefore not identified by an arbitrarily weighted null.
claims.plant_prominence_gradient: Exploratory SI result only: plant HOSTS degree covaries positively with redistribution but may reflect ecological prominence, recording intensity, and reverse causation.
claims.pgls_coverage_bias: Tree-matched species have higher expansion magnitude (median log expansion 0.376 vs 0.285; p=0.0012) but similar host-family breadth (median 2 vs 2; p=0.677). Breadth–expansion rho is near zero in both matched (-0.055) and unmatched (+0.053) groups. PGLS is used only for the slope sensitivity.
claims.equivalence_precision: Full-panel bootstrap 90% CI -0.092 to 0.108 and 95% CI -0.111 to 0.128. A post-hoc ±0.10 Fisher-z TOST is narrowly inconclusive (p=0.078). Do not claim exact zero or demonstrated ±0.10 equivalence.

claims.claim: The aggregate geographic opportunity added by introduced host distributions is strongly uneven across contributing host plants, and this concentration persists after host species are collapsed to genera.
claims.status: post-hoc descriptive decomposition elevated as a main ecological result; unit-preserving and non-causal
claims.evidence: 14,553 added butterfly×WGSRPD3 units across 206 expanded butterflies; 670 contributing host species and 431 contributing genera.
claims.key_statistic: Species level: top 10=25.1%, top 50=57.0%, 38/670 species reach 50%, Gini=0.777, effective contributors=92.5. Genus level: top 10=28.7%, top 50=67.0%, 25/431 genera reach 50%, Gini=0.774, effective contributors=69.9. Seven of the top ten species-level contributors are Poaceae.
claims.allowed_use: Describe which resources generate reconstructed added opportunity. Do not infer causal plant traits, independent plant-level effects, realized larval use, or introduction pathways.

claims.claim: Introduced host ranges recover contemporary butterfly occurrence units lying beyond native-host geography more often than expected from structural overlap.
claims.status: secondary occurrence validation using the pre-existing climate-stratified panel, with post-hoc structural and species-cluster nulls
claims.evidence: 32-species climate-stratified panel used secondarily for occurrence validation; 23 species had outside-native occurrence units.
claims.key_statistic: 66/115 outside-native species×WGSRPD3 units recovered (57.4%); species-level mean recovery=0.583 vs region-matched null median=0.385 with 0/99,999 exceedances; excluding Pyrgus communis leaves 44/93=47.3% vs null median 30 units with 0/99,999 exceedances

claims.claim: The apparent specialist-generalist gradient in host-contribution concentration is largely explained by structural constraints imposed by resolved host-species richness.
claims.status: post-hoc structural diagnostic retained in Supplementary Information
claims.key_statistic: raw rho=0.492/-0.486; exact-host-count-adjusted r=0.059/-0.071 with p=0.502/0.415; joint host-count+butterfly-Family r=-0.039/+0.015
claims.allowed_use: Supplementary structural diagnostic/caution only; not a headline mechanism or main-text results section.

claims.claim: Climate-associated filtering is common within contemporary host-resource opportunity and persists after geographic-distance controls.
claims.status: independent cross-fit descriptive result with post-hoc spatial sensitivities

claims.claim: The pre-specified prediction that broader host-family diets weaken climate filtering was not supported and remains imprecisely estimated.
claims.status: independent directional hypothesis test + post-hoc precision diagnostic
claims.key_statistic: partial rho=-0.166; one-sided p=0.2237; bootstrap 95% interval -0.583 to 0.261; approximate 80%-power MDE |rho|≈0.505

forbidden_overclaims: Introduced host distributions caused butterfly range expansion.
A recovered butterfly occurrence proves local larval use of an introduced host.
Every reconstructed introduced-host region is currently used by the butterfly.
The occurrence overlap null establishes causality.
Butterfly Family adjustment is equivalent to PGLS.
Host-family breadth has exactly zero effect on proportional expansion or climate filtering.
Climate alone determines realized butterfly distributions.
The raw specialist-generalist portfolio-concentration gradient is an independent biological mechanism.
The matched-host null proves that butterflies evolved to use globally redistributed plants.
The 32-species panel was prospectively designed as an occurrence-validation panel.
Actual butterfly host identities produce excess anthropogenic expansion after controlling plant native-range breadth and network-wide host prominence.
Network-wide host use proves ecological commonness rather than HOSTS recording intensity.
Host-family breadth has been demonstrated equivalent to a zero effect within ±0.10.
The host-contribution concentration analysis identifies causal plant traits or independent plant-level effects.
Poaceae membership explains why the leading host plants were redistributed.

required_language.resource_geography: Use reconstructed or potential resource opportunity, not realized butterfly range.
required_language.occurrence_validation: State that the 32-species panel was originally stratified for the climate test and reused secondarily for occurrence validation. Do not describe it as a prospectively designed or independent validation panel. Report species-cluster and leave-one-out robustness, including Pyrgus communis.
required_language.anthropogenic: Attribute resource-envelope expansion to introduced host distributions, not causal butterfly expansion.
required_language.architecture: Describe raw concentration patterns as structurally constrained and secondary.
required_language.climate: Use climate-associated filtering language, not proof of physiological causation.
required_language.negative_primary: State that the directional climate-release prediction was not supported and was imprecisely estimated, not that the effect is zero.
required_language.matched_host_null: Treat the simple same-family matched-host excess as an intermediate result only. Follow it with the parameter-sensitivity result: attenuation depends on how plant prominence is represented, so the analysis does not identify a butterfly-specific host-choice effect or a unique prominence-mediated decomposition.
required_language.host_bias_null: Describe other-Lepidoptera consumer count as a joint proxy for host prominence and recording intensity. Do not say that one strict null proves the host-identity excess disappears; the 3×3 grid shows that inference varies with prominence-weight strength.
required_language.host_prominence: Treat network prominence only as an exploratory explanatory hypothesis in Discussion/SI. Do not put it in the title, abstract main conclusion, or causal interpretation; HOSTS degree is Lepidoptera-wide and may be affected by recording intensity and reverse causation.
required_language.host_bias_parameter_sensitivity: Keep the 3×3 weighting grid in SI. In the main text, state only that host-identity excess is sensitive to how network prominence is represented and therefore is not interpreted as a butterfly-specific mechanism.
required_language.phylogeny: State that the Kawahara exact-match subset is selective for higher expansion magnitude. Because fitted Pagel lambda is 0.033, present the estimated-lambda model as the data-adaptive phylogenetic correction and fixed Brownian lambda=1 as a boundary sensitivity; do not imply that Brownian beta=0.140 excludes a moderate positive effect.
required_language.diet_breadth_equivalence: Use 'little relationship', 'near-zero point estimate', or 'largely independently'. State that the 49,999-bootstrap 95% CI is -0.111 to 0.128 and that a post-hoc ±0.10 TOST is narrowly inconclusive (p=0.078). Do not claim an exact zero effect or demonstrated ±0.10 equivalence.
required_language.host_contribution_concentration: Describe the decomposition as contribution-weighted and unit-preserving: 14,553 added butterfly×WGSRPD3 units are divided among contributing hosts. Species-level and genus-level concentration are descriptive main results; they identify which resources generate reconstructed opportunity, not why those plants were redistributed.
